# Task: Support property-to-property comparisons in Cypher WHERE clauses

## Problem

The Cypher query subset supported by `src/cypher/cypher.c` fails to parse a WHERE condition that compares one variable's property with another variable's property. The query aborts with `expected value at pos N` at the right-hand operand.

Examples that fail on the current code:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.name <> b.name RETURN a.name, b.name
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name
```

Property-to-literal comparisons already work and must keep working:

```
MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE b.file_path = 'demo.go' RETURN a.name, b.name
```

## Required behavior

Extend the WHERE parser and evaluator so that when the right-hand side of a comparison operator is another `variable.property` expression (not a string/number/boolean literal), the condition compares the two resolved property values for the current binding.

1. `a.prop = b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values are equal.
2. `a.prop <> b.prop` — true when the two resolved string values differ.
3. All existing comparison operators that make sense on property values (`>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`) should also accept a property right-hand side, evaluated the same way as when the right-hand side is a numeric literal (via `strtod`).
4. The property right-hand side must resolve through the same binding mechanism used for the left-hand side (`node_prop` / bare-alias name), so File, Function, and other node property paths all work.
5. Property-to-literal and bare-alias comparisons must continue to work exactly as before.
6. The change must work in both the early WHERE (after MATCH) and post-WITH WHERE paths, since they share the same parser and evaluator.

## Where to change

- Parser: `parse_condition_expr` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently rejects a non-literal right-hand side with `expected value at pos %d`.
- Condition model: `cbm_condition_t` in `src/cypher/cypher.h` currently only stores a literal `value`.
- Evaluator: `eval_condition` / `resolve_condition_value` in `src/cypher/cypher.c` currently resolve only the left-hand side against the binding.

## Constraints

- Do not break any existing Cypher behavior (WHERE with literals, regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT).
- Keep the error path for genuinely unsupported right-hand sides (e.g. function calls on the RHS if not already supported) clear and non-crashing.
- Add unit tests in the existing Cypher test suite covering property-to-property `=`, `<>`, and at least one ordering operator, plus a WITH-path case.
- The full project test suite (`make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test`) must still pass.

## How to verify

```sh
make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli index_repository '{"repo_path":"/tmp/demo","mode":"full","name":"demo"}'
./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph '{"project":"demo","query":"MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name"}'
```

Before the fix this errors with `expected value at pos N`. After the fix it returns only CALLS edges whose source and target files are the same.

activities.objective:
Extend the Cypher engine so a WHERE comparison's right-hand side may be another `variable.property` (property-to-property comparison). Target files: src/cypher/cypher.h, src/cypher/cypher.c, tests/test_cypher.c.

1) Condition model (cypher.h:185, cbm_condition_t): add `const char *rhs_variable;` and `const char *rhs_property;` (NULL = literal RHS, preserving current layout semantics). Extend the comment on `op` to note `value` holds the literal OR the RHS literal while `rhs_variable`/`rhs_property` hold a property RHS. Ensure cbm_query_free's condition teardown (search for safe_str_free of condition fields in cypher.c) frees both new fields when set.

2) Parser (parse_condition_expr, cypher.c ~1080-1095): after `c.op = parse_comparison_op(p)`, if the next token is TOK_IDENT and the token after it is TOK_DOT followed by a TOK_IDENT, consume all three and set c.rhs_variable / c.rhs_property via heap_strdup (mirroring the LHS parse at cypher.c:1040-1051). Accept the property RHS only for ops: "=", "<>", ">", "<", ">=", "<="; for any other op (regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, IN, IS NULL...) with an IDENT RHS, fall through to the existing 'expected value at pos %d' error path (keep error message and cleanup identical). Bare IDENT without a following DOT must keep the current 'expected value' error. The change is in the shared parse_condition_expr so both the post-MATCH WHERE and post-WITH WHERE paths get it for free.

3) Evaluator (cypher.c ~2331-2466): generalize resolve_condition_value (or add a helper) so the same resolution logic (edge_prop for edges, node_prop(n, prop, store) for nodes, n->name for bare alias with NULL property) can resolve an arbitrary (variable, property) pair against a binding. In eval_condition, after the HAS_LABEL / EXISTS / IS NULL / IS NOT NULL / IN early-returns (those ops never have a property RHS), when c->rhs_variable is set: resolve both actual (existing LHS path) and expected (rhs_variable/rhs_property). If actual is NULL keep the existing 'return true' behavior; if expected is NULL (unbound RHS variable), treat expected as "" so comparisons are well-defined and non-crashing. Then call eval_comparison_op(c->op, actual, expected) with the resolved RHS string instead of c->value. Ordering ops (>, <, >=, <=) already go through strtod inside eval_comparison_op — do not duplicate that logic.

4) Tests (tests/test_cypher.c): add TESTs in the existing harness style (see TEST(cypher_exec_where_label_test_issue241) at line 928 and the fixture builders near line 477 for how stores are built). Cover at minimum: (a) `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name` returning only same-file CALLS edges; (b) the same pattern with `<>` returning the complement; (c) one ordering operator (e.g. `a.start_line > b.start_line`) comparing two numeric props; (d) a WITH-path case: `MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WITH a, b WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name`; (e) regression: existing property-to-literal `WHERE b.file_path = "demo.go"` still works (add or reuse a fixture with CALLS edges — extend the test fixture with nodes/edges having file_path props if needed). Register all new TESTs in the main runner list (see RUN_TEST at line 2590).

Constraints: do not change behavior of any existing op (regex, CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, HAS_LABEL, EXISTS, AND/OR/XOR/NOT); keep the unsupported-RHS error path clear and non-crashing; no comments beyond what surrounding code style already does.

Verification: (1) `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= cbm` builds clean; (2) run the new tests plus the full suite `make -f Makefile.cbm SANITIZE= test` and report pass counts; (3) end-to-end smoke: index a tiny /tmp/demo repo and run `./build/c/codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph '{"project":"demo","query":"MATCH (a)-[:CALLS]->(b) WHERE a.file_path = b.file_path RETURN a.name, b.name"}'` — must return results, not 'expected value at pos N'.
